study_identification_part.si_3_author_journal_year: Ge et al., Lancet Digital Health, 2024
study_identification_part.si_4_title: Normative modelling of brain morphometry across the lifespan with CentileBrain: algorithm benchmarking and model optimisation

nm2_1_modeling_methods.detail: Eight algorithms were compared for normative modeling. MFPR (Multivariate Fractional Polynomial Regression) emerged as the preferred algorithm due to its combined advantages in accuracy and computational efficiency. Other algorithms tested include: OLSR, BLR, GAMLSS (including LMS subclass), GPR, WBLR, and HBR. The optimal models were sex-specific and region-specific models based on MFPR with non-linear fractional polynomials of age and linear effects of global neuroimaging measures.
nm2_1_modeling_methods.supporting_text: Accordingly, the MFPR emerged as the preferred algorithm given its combined advantages in accuracy and computational eﬃciency.; the optimal models as the sex-specific and region-specific models that were based on the MFPR algorithm with non-linear fractional polynomials of age and linear eﬀects of the appropriate global neuroimaging measure

nm2_2_response_variable.detail: Regional cortical thickness and cortical surface area measures (Desikan-Killiany atlas) and subcortical volumetric measures (Aseg atlas).
nm2_2_response_variable.supporting_text: measures of cortical thickness and cortical  surface  area  from  the  68  Desikan-Killiany  atlas regions and 14 subcortical volumetric measures based on the Aseg atlas.

nm2_3_explanatory_variables.detail: Base models used age as the explanatory variable; optimisation added site handling plus scanner vendor, FreeSurfer version, Euler number, and global measures (intracranial volume, mean cortical thickness, mean cortical surface area).
nm2_3_explanatory_variables.supporting_text: The potential effect of site on performance  was addressed both by handling site as a random factor and by  site-harmonisation  using  ComBat-GAM 19 and  then comparing the resulting models.; The  models  were  trained  with  five-fold cross-validation (5F-CV) in the corresponding sex-specific training  subset,  with  age  being  the  only  explanatory variable.; Model optimisation involved the evaluation of improvements  in  the  MAE  (and  RMSE  and  explained variance) by adding the following explanatory variables: global neuroimaging measures (ie, intracranial volume, mean cortical thickness, or mean cortical surface area, as appropriate), and both linear and non-linear contributions from  these  variables  were  considered;  scanner  vendor type; FreeSurfer version; Euler's number for scan quality; and  combinations  of  these  variables.
